p: Gentiles: That is, nine nations which are around the land of Egypt.
Pharaohnecho king of Egypt: Read 2Ki 23:29,24:7, 2Ch 35:20.
Order ye the buckler and shield: He warns the Egyptians to prepare themselves for war.
Why have I seen them dismayed: The prophet had this vision of the Egyptians who would be put to flight by the Babylonians at Carchemish.
north by the river Euphrates: The Babylonians will discomfit them at the river Euphrates.

a flood: He derides the boastings of the Egyptians, who thought by their riches and power to have overcome all the world, alluding to the Nile river, which at certain times overflows the country of Egypt.
the Cushites and the Libyans: For these nations took part with the Egyptians.
a sacrifice in the north country: He calls the slaughter of God's enemies a sacrifice, because it is a thing that pleases him, Isa 34:6.
by the river Euphrates: That is, at Carchemish.
and take balm: For at Gilead there grew a most sovereign balm for wounds.
daughter of Egypt: So called, because Egypt had not yet been overcome by the enemy.
medicines: He sows that no salve or medicine can prevail where God gives the wound.
own people: As they who would repent that they helped the Egyptians.
hath passed the time appointed: He derides them who blame their overthrow on lack of counsel and policy, or to fortune and not observing of time: not considering that it is God's just judgment.
he come: That is, that the Egyptians will be destroyed.
fair heifer: They have abundance of all things, and therefore are disobedient and proud.
are in the midst of her: As in Jer 46:9.
serpent: They will be scarcely able to speak for fear of the Chaldeans.
her with axes: Meaning Egypt.
her forest: That is, they will slay the great and mighty men of power.
That is, Nebuchadnezzar's army.
multitude of No: Some take the Hebrew word Amon for the kings name of No, that is, of Alexandria.
in the days of old: Meaning, that after forty years Egypt would be restored, Isa 19:23, Eze 29:13.

But fear not thou: God comforts all his that were in captivity but especially the small Church of the Jews, of which were Jeremiah and Baruch, who remained among the Egyptians: for the Lord never forsakes his, Isa 44:2, Jer 30:10.
thee in measure: Read Geneva "Jer 20:14"
